ddos_labeling_decision.reason: They are bounded controlled DDoS-like HTTP workloads from logical aliases on one physical VM, and E13 did not establish convergence to frozen training DDoS. They are useful diagnostic evidence, not scientifically adequate direct DDoS labels.

future_data_methodology: multiple independent traffic-generator nodes rather than logical aliases
raw PCAP, 84-column CSV, exact 78 matrix, and provenance preservation

Q1_PortScan_remediation.evidence: E6 RF-v2/RF-v3 PortScan recall 0/0.9993337775; E7 independent runtime recall 0/0.9983361065.
Q1_PortScan_remediation.limitation: One unseen PortScan runtime session and narrow tested scope.

Q2_Normal_preservation.evidence: Normal recall was 1.0 in E6 and E7; E13-N-R1 was 32/32 RF-v3 Normal.
Q2_Normal_preservation.scope: Only the tested Experiment E Normal sessions/profiles; not universal Normal performance.

Q3_DDoS_runtime_weakness.evidence: E10 was 0/802 DDoS; E13 D1 was 2/801 and D2 4/1612 RF-v3 DDoS on controlled DDoS-like profiles.
Q3_DDoS_runtime_weakness.scope: Very low sensitivity on the controlled DDoS-like runtime workloads evaluated, not universal DDoS recall.

Q4_RFv2_to_RFv3_regression_signal.evidence: Paired same-vector comparisons establish changed decisions and more RF-v2 DDoS classifications on these vectors.
Q4_RFv2_to_RFv3_regression_signal.not_proven: Universal model degradation or a causal class-boundary mechanism.

Q5_Workload_domain_mismatch.evidence: E12 and E13 all-78-feature scale-aware comparisons show material shifts from frozen E4 DDoS; D2 did not become closer than D1.
Q5_Workload_domain_mismatch.limitation: Association/distribution diagnostics do not identify the causal source of mismatch.

Q6_Pipeline_defect.evidence: E12 exact 802-vector reconstruction reproduced RF-v3 persisted classes/probabilities; E13 locked 84-to-78 reconstruction and model hashes passed.
Q6_Pipeline_defect.scope: No evidence that schema/order/extractor/model loading/dashboard serialization/runtime inference plumbing is the primary explanation in the analyzed evidence.

Q7_future_model_experiment.rationale: A new, separately preregistered three-class experiment is justified to preserve demonstrated PortScan/Normal gains while explicitly testing and improving DDoS behavior. This decision neither creates nor authorizes RF-v4.

demonstrated: RF-v3 materially corrected the scoped PortScan runtime-generalization failure and preserved Normal behavior in tested E6/E7/E13 scope.
RF-v3 had very low detection sensitivity on evaluated controlled DDoS-like runtime profiles.
must_not_claim: E10/E13 were real distributed DDoS attacks.
E10/E13 are directly suitable DDoS training labels.
RF-v4 has been created, trained, authorized, or promoted.
strongly_indicated: The paired RF-v2/RF-v3 evidence signals changed DDoS decision boundaries on recovered/evaluated vectors.
Runtime DDoS-like workloads materially differ from frozen E4 DDoS distributions.
unresolved: Mechanism and universality of DDoS weakness; broader lab-vs-training domain mismatch; performance on properly designed new DDoS ground truth.
